topic.title: Sinusoidal Function Context and Data Modeling
topic.summary: Building sinusoidal models of periodic phenomena: the period from consecutive maximums or minimums, the amplitude and midline from the extreme values, the phase shift from one data point, sinusoidal regression, and where a model can be trusted.

lesson.title: Sinusoidal Function Context and Data Modeling
lesson.summary: Building sinusoidal models of periodic phenomena: the period from consecutive maximums or minimums, the amplitude and midline from the extreme values, the phase shift from one data point, sinusoidal regression, and where a model can be trusted.
learningGoals: 3.7.A Construct sinusoidal function models of periodic phenomena.
lesson.bigIdea: A sinusoidal model needs four numbers, and data supply each one: the time between peaks gives the period, the peak and trough give the amplitude and midline, and one known point fixes the phase shift.
lesson.context: Topic 3.6 read features from an equation. Here the direction reverses: start from a context or a table, estimate the features, and write the equation, by hand or with a regression.

sections.title: 3.7.A · Period from consecutive extremes; amplitude and midline from the extreme values.
sections.conceptTitle: Period, amplitude, and vertical shift from data

blocks.text: The smallest interval of input values over which the maximum or minimum output values start to repeat, that is, the input-value interval between consecutive maxima or consecutive minima, can be used to determine or estimate the period and frequency for a sinusoidal function model.
The maximum and minimum output values can be used to determine or estimate the amplitude and vertical shift for a sinusoidal function model.

Example: at a harbor, high tide is 9.2 feet at 3:00 a.m. and the next low tide is 1.4 feet at 9:15 a.m. From a maximum to the next minimum is half a cycle, 6.25 hours, so the period is 12.5 hours and the frequency is 1/12.5 = 0.08 cycle per hour. The amplitude is (9.2 − 1.4)/2 = 3.9 feet and the midline is D = (9.2 + 1.4)/2 = 5.3 feet.

blocks.caption: From the tide data to the parameters of D(t) = a cos(b(t + c)) + d

sections.takeaway: Peak to peak is a period; peak to trough is half a period.

sections.title: 3.7.A · One data point fixes the phase shift; technology can do the fitting.
sections.conceptTitle: Phase shift, regression, and the contextual domain

blocks.text: An actual pair of input-output values can be compared to pairs of input-output values produced by a sinusoidal function model to determine or estimate a phase shift for the model.

For the tide, t is hours after midnight. Cosine reaches its maximum when its input is 0, and the real maximum is at t = 3, so the model needs b(t + c) = 0 at t = 3, which means c = −3. The model is D(t) = 3.9 cos(0.16π(t − 3)) + 5.3. Check: D(3) = 3.9 + 5.3 = 9.2 and D(9.25) = −3.9 + 5.3 = 1.4.

blocks.caption: The tide model D(t) = 3.9 cos(0.16π(t − 3)) + 5.3 for the first day
blocks.alt: A wave with maximums of 9.2 at t = 3 and t = 15.5 and a minimum of 1.4 at t = 9.25, with a dashed midline at 5.3.

blocks.text: Sinusoidal function models can be constructed for a data set with technology by estimating key values or using sinusoidal regressions. The calculator on this site fits y = a sin(b(x + c)) + d to a list of points; check its period and midline against the data before using it.

Sinusoidal functions that model a data set are frequently only useful over their contextual domain, can be used to predict values of the dependent variable from values of the independent variable, and may be used to determine values of the independent variable from values of the dependent variable.

blocks.title: Write it like the AP Exam
blocks.text: Based on the model, the depth is predicted to be D(6) ≈ 5.54 feet at 6:00 a.m. Because the model was built from one day of tides, it is less reliable for predictions weeks later, when the times of high and low tide drift.

sections.takeaway: Match one real point to fix c; trust the model mainly inside the data's domain.

vocabulary.definition: Sinusoidal function models can be constructed for a data set with technology by estimating key values or using sinusoidal regressions.

connections.title: Choosing and checking models
connections.body: Topic 2.6 compared models using residuals. A sinusoidal regression is checked the same way: residuals that look random support the model.
connections.transferQuestion: A sinusoidal model's residuals are all positive in the afternoon and all negative at night. What does that suggest?
connections.feedback: The model is systematically off at those times, so it can be improved, possibly by adjusting the phase shift.

connections.title: Solving with a model
connections.body: Finding when the tide reaches a given depth means solving D(t) = k, a trigonometric equation. Topic 3.10 solves these with inverse trigonometric functions.
connections.transferQuestion: Write the equation you would solve to find when the depth is 7 feet.

glossary.definition: The period of the function is the smallest positive value k such that f(x + k) = f(x) for all x in the domain. Consequently, the behavior of a periodic function is completely determined by any interval of width k.

A sinusoidal function is any function that involves additive and multiplicative transformations of f(θ) = sin θ. The sine and cosine functions are both sinusoidal functions, with cos θ = sin(θ + π/2).
The period and frequency of a sinusoidal function are reciprocals. The period of f(θ) = sin θ and g(θ) = cos θ is 2π, and the frequency is 1/(2π).
The amplitude of a sinusoidal function is half the difference between its maximum and minimum values. The amplitude of f(θ) = sin θ and g(θ) = cos θ is 1.

The midline of the graph of a sinusoidal function is determined by the average, or arithmetic mean, of the maximum and minimum values of the function. The midline of the graphs of y = sin θ and y = cos θ is y = 0.

The graph of the additive transformation g(θ) = sin(θ + c) of the sine function f(θ) = sin θ is a horizontal translation, or phase shift, of the graph of f by −c units. The same transformation of the cosine function yields the same result.
Sinusoidal function models can be constructed for a data set with technology by estimating key values or using sinusoidal regressions.
